- EU primary residency for production traffic (DACH + Benelux)

Hannah — thanks for the quick turnaround and the docs. A couple items from our side:

- Residency: Production must remain EU-resident for PHI processing per our legal guidance. Logs/metrics for observability can be replicated to APAC but must be redacted of user identifiers. Eventual replication is acceptable for that.
- Failover RTO: our ops lead wants a 15–30 minute target; anything above 30 minutes will require a different on-call posture.
- Timeline: we want a DACH MVP cutover before the end of Q3 (target week of 2028-09-18).

Also, we need clarity on cost delta for keeping warm standby in APAC versus cold standby (warmed on demand). Can you share the incremental monthly run rate for each option?

Best,

Subject: Re: Multi-region migration SOW & capacity addendum (EU primary, APAC standby)

Hi all —

Quick technical clarifications and proposal:

1) Residency & logs: We'll implement an ingestion routing policy so that inbound user content for PHI routes stays in the EU cluster (separate tenant routing). Observability data (traces/metrics) can be replicated to APAC after redaction at the edge. That matches "eventual replication" and avoids synchronous cross-border disk writes.

2) APAC standby options (cost delta estimates):
   - Cold standby (warmed on demand): baseline + ~15% monthly on reserved capacity for cold-reserve and orchestration.
   - Warm standby (pre-warmed VM/GPU pool with autoscale): baseline + ~55% monthly (keeps minimal workers ready).
   - Hot active-active (not requested): baseline + ~120% and additional ingress routing changes.

3) Failover RTO: We can achieve 15–30 minutes for critical routes with the canary cutover and prefix/KV cache priming in the runbook. The runbook includes preflight checks and a 20-minute hold for validation before full failover.

4) Timeline: For the DACH MVP week-of 2028-09-18 we recommend the following milestones:
   - 2028-07-10: finalize addendum & sign
   - 2028-07-24: infra prep in EU cluster (pre-provision GPUs, network allowlists)
   - 2028-08-14: APAC standby pool reservation and quantization profile validation
   - 2028-09-04: internal canary + security review
   - 2028-09-18: MVP cutover (canary -> promote)

I'll attach a pared-down runbook as a doc once we have the signed addendum — these dates assume we go with eventual replication for logs.

- Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Multi-region migration SOW & capacity addendum (EU primary, APAC standby)

Hi Lina —

Attached is a short capacity estimate and the incremental pricing that maps to the cold vs warm standby Karthik outlined. Key callouts:

- Cold standby: minimal monthly carry cost, higher per-minute spin-up during bursts. Good if Helio can tolerate a brief warm-up window beyond the failover validation window.
- Warm standby: higher baseline but consistent latency for burst traffic and a smoother operator experience.

Pricing summary (monthly incremental):
- Cold standby: +15% (~$12k/month on current committed)
- Warm standby: +55% (~$44k/month on current committed)

If you want, we can include a ramp credit for the first 3 months (50% on the incremental warm standby fee) as part of the renewal to smooth cost while you validate the MVP.

Marcus Lin
Capacity & Pricing | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com

Lina —

Thanks for the clarifications. Next steps to get this into your renewal:

1) I'll update the SOW to explicitly call out EU-resident processing for PHI routes and redacted observability replication to APAC.
2) We will add an addendum that includes the warm vs cold standby pricing options; Marcus proposed a 3-month ramp credit for warm standby (50% off incremental).
3) Monica will push the addendum to DocuSign once you confirm the standby option. (DocuSign link will be provided in the HubSpot deal.)

If you're OK with eventual replication for logs and targeting a 20-minute RTO for critical routes, we'll prepare the DocuSign today and lock the July 10 sign date to keep the timeline Karthik outlined.

Please reply with: "Accept warm standby ramp credit" or "Accept cold standby" and we will proceed.

Thanks —
Hannah
